1.explanation: Both the Show/Hide switch and the rotation‐style switch are implemented in these two components. In sprite-info.jsx the two <div className={styles.radio}> elements render the Show/Hide option and apply the styles.isActive class when props.visible is true or false. In direction-picker.jsx the three <button> elements for ALL_AROUND, LEFT_RIGHT, and DONT_ROTATE apply styles.active when their rotationStyle is selected. To fix the colorblind issue you will update these components’ CSS (sprite-info.css and direction-picker.css) to give the active .isActive/.active selectors a colored background and the inactive buttons a white background, rather than relying on icon tint alone.
1.bug_scenario: The Show/Hide toggle in the Sprite Info pane (and the rotation‐style buttons in the direction picker) currently indicate their “on”/“off” state solely by filling or graying out the icon. In the screen‐captures you provided, in full color you can tell “Show” is active because the eye icon is dark and “Hide” is gray. But when viewed in grayscale (or by colorblind users), both icons look equally gray and it’s impossible to tell which one is selected. The desired solution is to give the selected option a distinct background (e.g. a solid blue panel behind the active icon) and leave the inactive one with a white background, making the active choice obvious even without color.
